section_entries.label: 6. The natural approximation
section_entries.mathematical_role: Studies the uncorrected Möbius-weighted approximant, derives coordinate limits and tail control, and quantifies a low-coordinate mass obstruction.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Triangular square-summable-window criterion for RH
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Criterion 1 states that a uniform square-summable envelope only on p in [n+1,n^4] for infinitely many n closes the triangular approximation argument and implies RH. It precisely identifies the scheme's remaining burden after exact low-coordinate cancellation and automatic far-tail control.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Natural-approximation domination criterion
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Criterion 2 reduces RH for the natural approximants to a square-summable uniform coordinate envelope on p up to n^2 log n for infinitely many n. Compared with the triangular scheme the unresolved range is shorter at the top but includes all low coordinates.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Triangular correction, raw Möbius weighting, and exponent smoothing all solve fixed-coordinate convergence and admit automatic remote-tail control; they differ in exact low-coordinate cancellation and in the moving interval on which a common square-summable majorant remains necessary.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: All three RH conclusions are conditional on an unproved domination hypothesis for infinitely many n; coordinatewise limits and big-O tails alone do not give Hilbert-norm convergence.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The natural scheme's exact low-coordinate energy forces simultaneous cancellation in Möbius partial sums, revealing a concrete obstruction that the smoothed weights are designed to soften while preserving the same target coordinates.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The source does not prove that smoothing removes the unconditional obstruction; its strongest positive efficiency statement assumes RH and cites prior work.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Removing the triangular endpoint corrections reveals the raw Möbius mechanism: divisor cancellation still sends every fixed coefficient to the coordinates of -E1, and a simple scale estimate controls the far tail, but low and intermediate energy are no longer canceled exactly.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The natural approximant is sum_{q<=n} mu(q)e_q/q with coordinates y_{n,p}. Lemma 2, rearrangement of divisor sums, and the asymptotics of S_n and S'_n give y_{n,1}->-1 and y_{n,p}->0 for each fixed p>1. The source also obtains y_{n,p}=O(n/p), leading to a p-only square-summable bound for p>=n^2 log n.
directed.conceptual_reading: The raw arithmetic weights already solve coordinatewise targeting; the discarded endpoint corrections were serving global energy control rather than fixed-coordinate correctness. This exposes how a natural local rule can fail through migrating mass.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Divisor-sum cancellation converts Möbius weights into the correct fixed basis coordinates, while the estimate <e_q,E_p>=O(q/p) bridges generator scale to remote-frequency decay.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Coordinatewise convergence to -E1 and far-tail decay do not imply convergence in H. The unresolved range now includes low coordinates as well as the intermediate window.
directed.uncertainty: The target sign and threshold are clear. The extracted comparison symbol in the majorant is damaged, so its precise printed inequality should be PDF-verified.

section_entries.label: 7. Smooth approximations and acknowledgements
section_entries.mathematical_role: Introduces exponent smoothing, proves its coordinate limits and tail estimate under a decay window, and states the corresponding RH criterion and conditional comparison.

unit_result_entry.title: Exponent-smoothed Möbius approximation
unit_result_entry.why_material: Replacing mu(q)/q by mu(q)/q^(1+epsilon_n), with epsilon_n tending to zero no faster than the stated logarithmic threshold, preserves coordinatewise convergence to -E1 and the O(n/p) far-tail estimate. The proof rewrites divisor sums by Euler products and controls zeta-tail errors directly.

neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: An exact formula for the sum of y_{n,p}^2 over 2<=p<=n+1 converts success of Criterion 2 into simultaneous smallness conditions on two Möbius partial-sum combinations. The source argues these are quite restrictive and contrasts them with known square-root-scale oscillation, diagnosing why coordinatewise convergence alone is inadequate.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Smoothed domination criterion and conditional calibration
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Criterion 3 gives the smoothed analogue of Criterion 2: a square-summable envelope through n^2 log n along infinitely many n implies RH. The source reports that under RH prior work verifies the criterion for a particular logarithmic smoothing scale and even bounds the approximation distance, making this scheme a conditional calibration rather than an unconditional proof.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Exponent smoothing regularizes the raw Möbius weights just enough to control truncated Euler-product tails while letting the exponent return to the boundary value. The correct fixed coordinates and the same remote-tail decay survive this deformation.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The smoothed approximant uses coefficients mu(q)/q^(1+epsilon_n), where epsilon_n>=2 log log n/log n and epsilon_n=o(1). Proposition 7 rewrites divisor sums using Euler products for 1/zeta and its derivative, bounds the omitted q>n tails directly, and obtains y_{n,1}(epsilon_n)->-1 and y_{n,p}(epsilon_n)->0 for fixed p>1. It also retains y_{n,p}(epsilon_n)=O(n/p) and the remote bound beyond n^2 log n.
directed.conceptual_reading: The exponent is a tunable regularization parameter: positive smoothing makes arithmetic tails controllable, while epsilon_n->0 preserves the desired unsmoothed target. This is an Abel-type approach to a boundary object.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Dirichlet-series/Euler-product identities bridge smoothed Möbius sums to zeta near s=1, and explicit truncation estimates bridge the infinite identities back to finite approximants.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The proposition proves fixed-coordinate limits and far-tail control, not a common l2 bound on the remaining coordinates. Smoothing is motivated by the natural scheme's obstruction but is not shown here to remove it unconditionally.
directed.uncertainty: The extraction corrupts the epsilon glyph, though its lower bound and o(1) role are clear. Exact exponents and tail inequalities require PDF verification.

supported: The span introduces mu(q)/q^(1+epsilon_n), assumes epsilon_n>=2 log log n/log n and epsilon_n=o(1), uses reciprocal-zeta identities plus direct q>n tail estimates, and recovers the fixed-coordinate limits and remote-tail statement.
The candidate correctly leaves the common l2 domination on the remaining coordinates unproved and flags the corrupted epsilon glyph.
inference: An Abel-type approach toward the boundary s=1 is a meaningful mathematical analogy, but it is an interpretive label rather than source terminology.
unsupported_or_imported: “Just enough” suggests that the displayed lower bound is sharp or minimal; the proposition establishes it only as a sufficient decay window.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The regularization language is useful when tied to the explicit exponent and tail estimates, not presented as a proved optimal smoothing principle.
context_or_ocr_risk: The epsilon glyph, exponent typography, and comparison signs are damaged, so exact symbolic reuse requires scan verification.
